text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in container restarts (prefill path) on cluster gpu-prod-11. 90 restarts in last 5m. Suspected GPU OOM during prefill. Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/cluster/gpu-prod-11/query?from=now-10m

sre-oncall: saw it, paging oncall now. tagging eng-runtime + infra-lead.

alex: I can take first response. Can you post a short log snippet and the affected model/route?

incidents-bot: affected_route=\"/v1/generate\" model=\"rw-llama-30b-q4\" tenant=acct-842 region=us-west-2 container_restarts=92 prefill_oom=true stack:
```
2024-07-02T03:12:08Z ERROR runtime: cuda out of memory during prefill
    cudaError_t: 2 at /srv/runtime/prefill.cc:412
    KVCACHE_ALLOC failed size=2.1GB
    container restart: exit_code=137
```

maya: customer-impact? any 5xx seen at gateway?

sre-oncall: gateway metrics show 502 spike for tenant acct-842 between 03:11-03:18, ~120 failed requests. CS alerting customer.

cust-ops: customer reported degraded responses and timeouts for a batch job, they say it started after pushing a long-context job (600k tokens). They asked for ETA.

liam: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enable tenant-level prefill throttle (limit tokens/prefill) 2) move heavy requests to cold fallback model (cpu-quant) 3) evict large KV caches on that hotpool 4) temporary scale-up of hotpool GPUs.

eng-runtime: prepping a hotpatch to auto-throttle prefill if estimated prefill allocations > 8GB. Can flip a flag now: `./admin toggle --tenant acct-842 --prefill-throttle=on --limit=3GB`

infra-lead: before toggling — what's impact on latency? will requests be queued?

eng-runtime: throttle will short-circuit with 429 on new prefill requests exceeding limit (configurable backoff). Existing in-flight requests will be allowed to run; to avoid further restarts we should also drain new requests to that hotpool: `kubectl annotate pods -l pool=hotpool-11 maintenance=true` then route traffic elsewhere.

alex: do it. I'm running the toggle now and adding a sticky route to fallback pool.

alex: ran: `./admin toggle --tenant acct-842 --prefill-throttle=on --limit=3GB` -> OK

alex: annotated hotpool pods and updated routing rule to send acct-842 to fallback-hotpool-2 (lower-capacity, CPU-backed)

incidents-bot: Automation: created incident ticket INC-2024-9876 and annotated with mitigation steps.

maya: CS updated customer: "We observed GPU OOMs caused by a very large prefill; we've temporarily limited prefill size for your tenant and routed new jobs to a fallback pool to restore stability. We're working on a durable fix."

liam: observed container restarts dropping from ~20/min to ~1/min after change. Memory pressure trending down.

eng-runtime: followups: 1) add a prefill-size estimator in gateway to reject >X tokens earlier 2) improve KV eviction order for long contexts 3) add auto-evict policy when KVCACHE_ALLOC fails 4) longer-term: per-tenant quota UI in Console. I'll open JIRA tickets.

infra-lead: ops note: schedule maintenance to upgrade hotpool node types next week; consider packing improvements to reduce frag.

alex: handing off to night oncall @sre-oncall. summary pinned to channel and INC-2024-9876 updated with logs + runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/prefill-oom

sre-oncall: thanks — accepted handoff. Will monitor for 2h, then transition to eng-runtime for postmortem.

eng-runtime: quick snippet added to runbook for similar incidents: when prefill OOM on long-context -> throttle tenant, evict KV, route to fallback, collect heapdumps `/proc/heapdump` and upload.

cust-ops: customer confirmed partial restoration, will keep monitoring and asked for postmortem.

incidents-bot: incident state updated: mitigation=active, impact=partial, owners=[eng-runtime, infra-lead, sre-oncall], next_update=+30m. :white_check_mark:
